reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: One of the autosomal recessive HOXA1-spectrum disorders affecting hindbrain and cranial nerve development
Bilateral Duane retraction anomaly with limited horizontal eye movement is a hallmark ocular finding
Sensorineural hearing loss results from inner ear malformation with cochlear and labyrinthine hypoplasia
Internal carotid artery anomalies, including hypoplasia or absence, are an important vascular feature
Cardiac outflow tract and conotruncal defects may accompany the syndrome
Central hypoventilation and developmental delay occur in some individuals
It overlaps with Athabaskan brainstem dysgenesis, another HOXA1-related phenotype, differing partly by population and specific features
Diagnosis is confirmed by identification of biallelic HOXA1 variants
reference.pathophysiology: The disorder is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in HOXA1, a homeobox transcription factor expressed transiently in the developing hindbrain. HOXA1 is essential for patterning the rhombomeres of the embryonic brainstem, from which cranial nerve nuclei, inner ear structures, and adjacent vascular and cardiac derivatives arise. Loss of its function disrupts rhombomere identity and the subsequent development of the abducens-related ocular motor pathways, the cochlea and labyrinth, the internal carotid arteries, and the cardiac outflow tract. This unified developmental origin explains the co-occurrence of Duane retraction anomaly, sensorineural deafness, carotid malformation, and cardiac defects, transmitted in an autosomal recessive manner.
additionalDifferentials: Athabaskan brainstem dysgenesis, the related HOXA1-spectrum phenotype
Duane radial ray syndrome and isolated Duane retraction syndrome
Moebius syndrome with congenital facial and abducens palsy
CHARGE syndrome with cranial nerve and ear anomalies
Other causes of congenital sensorineural hearing loss with inner ear malformation
Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome of alternative cause
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of HOXA1 for biallelic variants
Audiological assessment and imaging of the inner ear
Neuro-ophthalmological evaluation for Duane retraction anomaly
Vascular imaging of the internal carotid arteries
Echocardiography for conotruncal and outflow tract defects
Assessment of respiratory control and developmental status
redFlags: Central hypoventilation with apnoea requiring respiratory support
Cerebrovascular compromise related to internal carotid artery anomaly
Profound hearing loss impairing communication development
reference.prognosis: Outlook depends heavily on the severity of associated cardiac, vascular, and respiratory involvement; deafness and the ocular motility limitation are stable and manageable, whereas central hypoventilation and major cardiovascular anomalies carry greater risk, and developmental outcome varies across the spectrum.
pitfalls: Attributing the Duane anomaly to an isolated eye disorder and missing the systemic HOXA1 syndrome
Overlooking internal carotid artery anomalies that carry cerebrovascular implications
Failing to assess respiratory control and thereby missing central hypoventilation
Not recognising autosomal recessive inheritance in counselling consanguineous families
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Hearing rehabilitation with hearing aids or cochlear implantation for sensorineural deafness from cochlear and labyrinthine hypoplasia
Neuro-ophthalmological management of Duane retraction anomaly, reserving strabismus surgery for an anomalous head posture or significant primary-position deviation
Cardiology surveillance with surgical repair of conotruncal and outflow-tract defects as required
Respiratory support for central hypoventilation, including sleep studies and assisted ventilation where indicated
Developmental support through early intervention, physiotherapy and speech and language therapy
Caution with the internal carotid artery anomalies during anaesthesia and any head or neck surgery, guided by vascular imaging
Coordinated multidisciplinary follow-up across clinical genetics, ENT, ophthalmology, cardiology and neurology
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance with carrier testing of parents and family screening
